sources.title: Egyptian Math: Part 1
sources.presenter: Seth Fleishman / World History by a Jew

anchors.reading: The lecture lists arithmetic, geometry, algebra, multiplication, division, fractions and square roots, then introduces land measurement as an application.
The lecture describes Nile-height measurement, harvest estimation and taxation as practical measurement contexts.
The presenter previews a second part on geometry, tools, rope measurement and worked Egyptian calculations.

sources.title: Ancient Egyptian Math Is Modern Computing?

arithmeticAudit.assessment: The source slide's 52.3 cm is a rounded display reading and is not exactly equal to 20 9/16 international inches. Primecube therefore keeps 0.523 m as a named Owner-intake view factor rather than an exact historical conversion standard.

claimBoundary: The two videos are secondary educational sources. The first supplies general historical-mathematics context but no cubit-length statement in the supplied transcript. The second supplies an Owner-observed visual reading without a transcript. Neither establishes one universal Egyptian cubit, a dimensional resonance system, a physical conversion mechanism or a new NEXAH relation.
